newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MIH Holdings share dips on poor yr earnings.
newsitem.headline: MIH Holdings share dips on poor yr earnings.

text.p: Shares in South African television subscription firm MIH Holdings Ltd dipped slightly on Tuesday after the company reported poor earnings for the year ended March 31, dealers said.
By about 1144 GMT the stock had lost five cents to 17.60 rand with around 10,500 shares worth around 185,105 rand traded on the counter.
"Their results show that they (MIH) are still making a loss and I think that's basically just the reason why they are down," one dealer said.
"The results were not particularly a good set of results," the dealer added.

MIH on Monday reported a loss of 196.6 cents in its headline earnings per share from 121.2 cents in the previous year, while its attributable earnings per share showed a gain at 854.1 cents versus 27.8 cents previously. But the results had been boosted by a net profit of 2.5 billion rand from the Canal Plus SA European merger.

The dealers added, however, that the market's lerthagic swing after a long weekend which sent volumes plummetting on Monday ahead of the June futures close out on Friday had also weighed in on the stock.
